summary.text: 包 means “wrap” or “pack” and can also mean a package or bundle. Its received form has traditionally been read as a pregnant figure enclosing an unformed child, though a competing origin proposal remains unresolved.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. The traditional reading of the received graph sees pregnancy: an enclosing outer form around an unformed child. Another analysis treats 勹 as enclosure and as a sound component. A competing proposal derives 包 from a separate graph depicting a person holding a child, which it says first wrote 抱; no dated forms establish that descent.

components.text: In the traditional interpretation of the received form, 巳 represents the unformed child within a pregnant figure. This identification is not established for the earliest graph.
In analyses of the received form, 勹 contributes the idea of enclosure and is proposed as a sound component. Neither role is established for the earliest formation.

sound.text: Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction assigns *pruː to both 勹 and 包, supporting the proposed sound link in that system. These are reconstructed values, not recorded ancient pronunciations.

history.text: The selected seal-script-style image is a modern redraw of the received graph. It shows the form associated with the traditional pregnancy interpretation, but does not document a dated stage in the character’s graphic history.

A competing proposal links 包 to oracle-bone graphs traditionally read as 保, interpreting them instead as a person holding a child and proposing that 包 first wrote 抱. The proposed link has no dated intermediate forms.

uncertainties.text: The traditional pregnancy interpretation and the proposed descent from a child-holding graph are competing accounts. The earliest form and its graphic history remain unresolved.
Enclosure and sound are proposed roles for 勹 in analyses of the received form; the sound comparison supports the phonetic analysis but does not establish its role in the earliest formation.
The seal-script-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image, and its correspondence to a primary historical record has not been verified.

senses.text: The traditional Shuowen account gives pregnancy as the meaning and interprets the inner element as an unformed child. This records a historical interpretation, not proof of the graph’s earliest meaning.

senses.period: Transmitted classical texts; written-witness dating unresolved
senses.text: Transmitted examples cited in later dictionaries use 包 for wrapping or containing, including the Shijing line 白茅包之. The date of the written witness is unresolved.
包 is used for a package or bundle as well as for wrapping and packing. The history of this object sense is undated.

developments.text: The package and bundle senses may extend the verb sense, but the available evidence does not show when or how this development occurred.

limitations.text: The proposal that 包 first wrote 抱 belongs to a disputed account of the graph’s origin; it is not an established, dated earliest meaning. Reported substitutions such as 包 for 苞 or 庖 do not establish the character’s original formation.
Later senses including encompassing, taking responsibility, and guaranteeing are recorded, but no dated sequence connects them to earlier senses.
Pregnancy and wrapping are recorded separately; the evidence does not establish whether one sense developed from the other.

overview.text: 包 means “wrap” or “pack” and can name a package or bundle. The traditional picture of pregnancy is one reading of its received form; its earliest graphic origin remains unresolved.

components.text: The traditional reading sees 巳 as an unformed child inside a pregnant figure; this identification is not established for the earliest graph.
勹 is read as enclosure and proposed as a sound component in the received form; its role in the earliest graph remains unsettled.

relationships.text: In the traditional reading of the received form, 巳 depicts an unformed child; the competing proposal does not establish it as a component of the earliest graph.
Some analyses of the received form read 勹 as contributing enclosure, consistent with the traditional account. Its role in the earliest formation is unsettled.
Analyses propose 勹 as a sound component. Zhengzhang reconstructs 勹 and 包 with the same value, but this does not settle 勹’s role in the earliest graph.
